title: JSON Logs Migration Guide
summary: Heads-up on dual ingestion of log bodies during the migration to native JSON storage in SigNoz
body_markdown:
# JSON Logs Migration Guide


Last Updated: November 03, 2026


2 min read


## 📌 Overview


SigNoz is moving log bodies from a string column (` body


`


) to native JSON storage (` body_v2


`


). Every field in the body becomes queryable by path, so log queries are faster and you can filter, group by and aggregate on body fields without a pipeline.


> **Track this migration in[SigNoz/signoz#13376](https://github.com/SigNoz/signoz/issues/13376)** for more details.


## 🔍 Why We Are Migrating


String bodies are parsed at query time on every matching row. With ClickHouse's native[JSON type](https://clickhouse.com/blog/a-new-powerful-json-data-type-for-clickhouse) , log queries ran about 30% faster and scanned about 99% less data in our benchmarks ([deep dive](https://signoz.io/blog/building-a-high-performance-log-store/) ).


## 📦 Dual Ingestion


During the transition, the collector writes each log body to both columns. Existing dashboards, alerts and saved views keep reading` body


`


, so you don't need to do anything yet.


## ⚙️ Resource Impact


Plan for this extra capacity before upgrading.


Component Resource Recommendation


OTel Collector CPU Keep 25% headroom


OTel Collector Memory Keep 25% headroom


ClickHouse CPU Keep 15% headroom


ClickHouse Disk Grow the logs volume by the size of` body


`


(query below)


To estimate the extra disk, run this on ClickHouse. The logs table will grow by about` body_pct


`


:


```text
SELECT
formatReadableSize(sumIf(column_data_compressed_bytes, column   =   'body'  ))   AS   body_size,
formatReadableSize(  sum  (column_data_compressed_bytes))   AS   table_size,
round  (  100   *   sumIf(column_data_compressed_bytes, column   =   'body'  )   /   sum  (column_data_compressed_bytes),   1  )   AS   body_pct
FROM   system  .  parts_columns
WHERE   database   =   'signoz_logs'   AND   table   =   'logs_v2'   AND   active;
```


The increase builds up gradually and reaches its full size one retention period after the upgrade.
